Where should Austin add homes—and how can more residents afford to stay?

On October 13, the City Council’s Housing and Planning Committee recommended a resolution to update Austin’s Strategic Housing Blueprint.

The original plan was adopted in 2017 and reaches the end of its ten-year horizon in 2027. Staff described an update looking ahead to 2037.

The proposed work includes:

• New goals for building and preserving housing
• Strategies to help prevent displacement
• Housing stability for renters and owners
• Planning around infrastructure, jobs and population growth

The draft also calls for the updated blueprint to inform a potential 2028 bond program.

Why it matters: This process could help shape where Austin directs housing resources and which needs receive priority. The draft highlights shortages of deeply affordable homes, family-sized units and housing in areas with strong access to opportunity.

This was a committee recommendation to the full Council—not adoption of a finished plan, a zoning change or approval of a bond election.

Sources: City of Austin, October 13, 2026—committee meeting, transcript and draft resolution.
